chunks: Al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalhub from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"Do not slaughter your sacrificial animals except by people of your religion, and do not give charity from your sacrifices except to Muslims, and give charity with what is other than the sacrifices (i.e., non-sacrificial food), excluding Zakat, to the People of the Covenant."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.نُسُكُكُمْ: Your sacrifices (specifically the animal slaughtered for ritual purposes)

ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive charity from sacrificial meat according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes a distinction between the ritual validity of the sacrifice, which requires the slaughterer to be from the same faith, and the permissibility of distributing its meat to non-Muslims, which is restricted to Muslims. It further clarifies that while obligatory Zakat is reserved for specific categories, voluntary charity (Sadaqah) can be extended to the Ahl al-Dhimma, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the purity and social utility of sacrificial meat. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of sacrifices within Tahdhib al-Ahkam, illustrating the practical application of religious identity in ritual acts.
